children.text: Fill in the bracketed fields, review with the clinic's Privacy Officer and Security Officer, and keep the signed copy with the compliance records for at least six years. Legal review is recommended before adoption.

items: Read modules 1 to 7 (about 20 minutes).

Complete the knowledge check. A score of 8 out of 10 or better is required; retake it if needed. Signed-in staff complete it online at ai.helixona.com/documentation/workforce-training, where the score is recorded automatically; the paper version below is the alternative. The assistant stays locked, for administrators too, until the check is passed and the acknowledgment signed (or a paper completion is recorded by an administrator).
Sign the acknowledgment: online, after passing the check, or on the last page of this document, returned to the Privacy Officer.
The training log in the Administration page records every online completion; the Privacy Officer adds paper completions to it.

runs: HIPAA is the federal law that protects patients' health information. It applies to Helixona and to each of us as members of its workforce. Protecting that information is part of the care we give: patients share it with us because they trust us. The same law sets penalties for the clinic and, in serious cases, for individuals, when information is mishandled. California adds its own rules (the Confidentiality of Medical Information Act) that reinforce the same duties.
This training covers one system, the Helixona Assistant. The clinic's general HIPAA training still applies to everything else you do.

children.text: Module 2. What counts as protected health information

runs: Protected health information (PHI) is any information that identifies a patient and relates to their health, care or payment. It is PHI whether it is on paper, on a screen or in a file. Examples of identifiers:

items: Name, address, phone number, email
Dates: birth, appointment, admission, service, death
Medical record, account, policy, claim and member numbers
Photos, signatures, voice
Anything else that could identify the person when combined with health or payment information

runs: if a stranger reading it could work out who the patient is, it is PHI. Treat it that way.

children.text: Module 3. What the Helixona Assistant is, and is not

runs: The Helixona Assistant is the clinic's private way to use Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic. It runs in the clinic's own cloud account, both Amazon Web Services and Anthropic have signed HIPAA agreements with the clinic, and every conversation and file stays under the clinic's control. It is approved for patient information.

children.text: The assistant is a capable drafting and analysis aid. It can also be confidently wrong. You are responsible for what you use and send.

items: https://ai.helixona.com. Use no other address. If the browser shows a security warning, stop and tell the Security Officer.
at least 12 characters with upper and lower case letters, a number and a symbol. Never reuse it anywhere else.
at your first sign-in you scan a QR code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password or Authy. From then on you enter the 6-digit code from the app after your password.
tell the Security Officer the same day. An administrator resets your authenticator and you enroll again at the next sign-in.
you are signed out after 15 minutes without activity. On a shared computer, sign out yourself when you step away.
use the link on the sign-in page. A code is sent to your work email.

runs: Include only the patient information the task needs. Summarizing one patient's EOB does not need the other nine patients on the same statement. Redact or split the file first.
Check names, dates, amounts, claim numbers and reasons against the source document before you use or send anything. If the assistant says it is unsure, treat that as a flag to verify.
You can attach PDF, TXT, MD and CSV files. Attach only what the task needs. Files are stored with the conversation and deleted with it.

A project gives every conversation in it the same instructions and reference files. A private project is yours; a project shared with the clinic is visible to every staff member. Do not put patient information in a shared project's name, description, instructions or files unless everyone needs it.
Conversations are deleted automatically after 30 days. Delete them sooner when the work is finished. Keep results only in the clinic's approved systems, never on personal devices or personal email.
Patient information goes into the Helixona Assistant and nowhere else. Consumer AI chatbots, translation websites and personal accounts are not approved, even if you delete the chat afterwards.
Report to the Security Officer within one hour if you notice, or even suspect, any of these:

items: A lost or stolen phone, laptop or authenticator
A sign-in you did not make, or a code request you did not trigger
An email or message asking for your password or code, even if it looks like it comes from the clinic
Patient information sent or shown to the wrong person
Patient information in a place it should not be, such as a shared project
Anything else that feels wrong

runs: Reporting a suspected incident is never penalized. Do not investigate or delete anything yourself; the Security Officer needs the trail intact.

Violating the clinic's policies, for example sharing an account, entering patient information into an unapproved tool, or looking at a patient's information without a work reason, results in sanctions from retraining up to termination, and may involve legal penalties. The policies exist to protect patients and to protect you.

runs: Choose one answer per question. Passing score: 8 of 10.
A coworker is out sick and asks you to sign in with your account so they can finish a letter. What do you do?
A. Share the code once. B. Decline; accounts are personal and an administrator can create one for them. C. Sign in for them on your computer.
Which of these is PHI?
A. A patient's name next to an appointment date. B. The clinic's address. C. A blank claim form.
You need the assistant to summarize one patient's EOB. The PDF you have covers ten patients. What is the right step?
A. Upload the whole file. B. Upload only the pages for that patient, or redact the others. C. Paste all ten into the message.
The assistant drafts an appeal letter with a claim number and denial code. Before sending it you must:
A. Send it; the assistant is accurate. B. Check the claim number, dates and reasons against the source document. C. Ask the assistant if it is sure.
Which tool may receive patient information?
A. Any AI chatbot with a good privacy policy. B. Only the Helixona Assistant at ai.helixona.com. C. Your personal account on a consumer AI product, if you delete the chat afterwards.
Your phone with the authenticator app is stolen on Saturday. When do you report it?
A. Monday morning. B. The same day, to the Security Officer. C. Only if you notice unusual activity.
How long are conversations kept?
A. Forever. B. 30 days after the last activity, or until you delete them. C. Until the end of the year.
You notice a conversation in a shared project that contains a patient's full record for no work reason. What do you do?
A. Ignore it. B. Report it to the Security Officer within an hour. C. Delete it yourself and say nothing.
You are on a shared front-desk computer and step away for lunch. What do you do first?
A. Nothing; the screen locks eventually. B. Sign out of the assistant. C. Close the browser tab only.
Who is responsible for a clinical or billing decision made using the assistant's output?
A. The assistant. B. Anthropic. C. The licensed staff member who reviews and uses it.
